correctness.rationale: The mathematical proof directly constructs the unique profile embedding for rigid finite Dedekind actions. Normality makes an oversized word stabilizer produce a genuine nontrivial equivariant automorphism; identical profiles in distinct orbits permit a colour-preserving exchange. The converse follows from profile invariance. A bijection with shift-orbit subsets proves the complete polynomial, unique sharp capacity and complement symmetry; exact stabilizer counts follow from finite subgroup Möbius inversion. The one-colour S3 example shows necessity of a hypothesis. The supplied checker independently corroborates multiple abelian groups and nonabelian Dedekind Q8, but finite computation is not a proof of the all-group claim.

originality.rationale: Credited the 2026 cofree full-shift functor, adjunction and Burnside orbit counts as prior work. Checked actual published group-action, unary-function and asymmetric-colouring results under the closest equivalences and broader settings. Cyclic primitive-necklace cases, automorphism-marking framework, and ordinary subgroup-inversion tools are credited antecedents, not separate novel claims. No inspected accessible full statement implies the all-Dedekind colour-profile theorem and rigid polynomial. Priority remains provisional; possible cofree-action equivalences are residual risks.
residual_risks: A more general categorical result on cofree G-sets or automorphism-free pointed actions may imply the classification without this wording.
Specialized subgroup-Möbius or generalized necklace tables may already state the exact polynomial.
The motivating 2026 paper was inspected in relevant public sections but not independently checked line-by-line through every appendix.
The related August 2026 cofree-functor paper establishes foundational shift and orbit counting statements; the rigidity corollaries could conceivably be viewed as a standard further consequence.
The same-model proof assessment is not an independent mathematical or historical-priority audit.

value.rationale: For an entire natural structural class, the theorem gives a canonical rigidity test, finite sharp maximum q^|G|, exact subgroup-sensitive polynomial of every rigid cardinality and labelled count, distinguishing C4 and C2×C2. The finite-size gaps and explicit non-Dedekind boundary are mathematically natural phenomena not just arbitrary finite computations; no downstream theorem is asserted.
